slides.h1: Retrograde Mercury and Your Calendar: Review Beats Launch
slides.sub: Why traditional timing favours re-doing over starting.

slides.body: Retrograde (vakri) is when a planet appears to move backwards from Earth. It is an optical effect of orbits, not Mercury actually reversing.
Mercury is the karaka (significator) of communication, contracts, travel logistics and trade. Traditional muhurta (timing) advice is to be careful with fresh starts in these areas.
A launch window is for signing, announcing and beginning. A review window is for revisiting, editing, auditing and finishing what already exists.

slides.h2: Good uses of a review window
points: Audit contracts before signing anything new
Revisit old drafts and unfinished projects
Delay non-urgent launches if you can
Do not cancel what is urgent
Treat it as a prompt to be careful

slides.body: This is a planning heuristic, not a law. Real deadlines still matter, and no retrograde decides your result. Check your own chart before drawing conclusions.
